articles.title: Alex Murdaugh wants murder indictments dismissed, saying agent lied to grand jury
articles.summary: Attorneys for Alex Murdaugh are expected in court Friday to ask a judge to throw out the original murder indictments for killing his wife and son.
articles.body: Attorneys for Alex Murdaugh are expected in court Friday to ask a judge to throw out the original murder indictments for killing his wife and son. Now they’re saying the chief investigator in the case lied to the grand jury. Murdaugh is facing a retrial on the murder charges after the South Carolina Supreme Court threw out his convictions and life sentence, ruling that a court clerk improperly influenced jurors against him during his 2023 trial. Even if the longshot request to dismiss the indictments is granted by Judge Debra McCaslin at Friday’s pretrial hearing, it may not stop or even postpone an April retrial for the disgraced lawyer. Prosecutors can seek another set of grand jury indictments as soon as next month, and defense attorneys said they won’t stop them. But a ruling for Murdaugh would be another rebuke of the chief investigator, State Law Enforcement Division agent David Owen. A judge last year threw out a different murder case Owen was involved in because the dead woman’s mother told the agent about a suicide threat her daughter made days before she died that Owen never relayed to prosecutors or defense attorneys. Owen abruptly retired in 2024, not long after he was honored as State Law Enforcement Officer of the Year. Prosecutors said Murdaugh, 58, killed his wife, Maggie, and younger son, Paul, on their sprawling property in the South Carolina Lowcountry in 2021. Murdaugh is spending decades in prison for stealing millions of dollars from clients, and has admitted in court that he is a thief, insurance cheat, bad lawyer and longtime opioid addict. But he denies being a killer. Defense lawyers said that as prosecutors sought the indictments, Owen told the Colleton County grand jury that blood spatter was found on a T-shirt Murdaugh was wearing the night of the killings. An earlier report from state agents said there were no blood stains, and no such evidence was introduced at trial. Owen also told grand jurors that the same ammunition load of buckshot in one chamber and large birdshot in the other used to kill Paul Murdaugh was found loaded in weapons all over the Murdaugh property, which wasn’t the case. Prosecutors said they had plenty of other evidence supporting the murder charges, and wrote that “a single mistake is not bad faith.” Owen told grand jurors about the video Paul Murdaugh recorded in which Alex Murdaugh’s voice could be heard at the scene, contradicting his denials. Owen also told them about the family’s mounting debts and how Murdaugh’s schemes to steal from clients and his law firm were close to being discovered. But Murdaugh’s lawyers have repeatedly pointed out how little physical evidence prosecutors have — no DNA or blood was found splattered on Murdaugh or any of his clothes, even though the killings were at close range with powerful weapons that were never found. Prosecutors said Murdaugh killed his wife and son because he thought the sympathy generated by the killings would buy him time to cover up his thefts.

articles.title: Europe seeks seat at Ukraine peace talks but lacks unified voice
articles.summary: EU leaders believe a US-backed process will allow Moscow and Washington to decide the fate of a conflict.
articles.body:
European nations are debating who may be their representative in Russia-Ukraine peace talks while the continent’s leaders spar with Russia over their participation in future negotiations.

Whether Europe should be represented by one person or a team – and who should take on the role – was debated on Friday as leaders of the 27-nation European Union (EU) met at a summit in Dublin, Ireland. Senior EU officials and politicians have been suggested, but there is no consensus yet.

What the job might entail is also unclear and contested. However, EU leaders have broadly agreed on the need for Europe to join the ongoing trilateral negotiations between Washington, Kyiv and Moscow.

The EU is concerned that a United States-backed process will allow Moscow and Washington to decide the fate of a war that has embroiled the continent.

After talks in Moscow with Russian President Vladimir Putin on Thursday, US envoys said that Europe would join future negotiations – but the Kremlin appeared to slam the brakes on that plan, saying no decision had been made.

German ⁠Chancellor Friedrich Merz on Friday pleaded for ⁠US President Donald Trump to create no ⁠surprises during expected talks with Putin in China next week.

“Some here in Dublin fear this could turn into a ‘second Anchorage moment’,” ⁠said Merz on ⁠the sidelines of the EU meeting, a reference to the Alaska summit where they were stunned by Trump’s overtures to the Russian leader in the absence of Ukrainian or European envoys.

“I therefore ⁠want to state ⁠our message to ⁠the United States very clearly: please, no surprises. Continue ‌to play as part of ‘Team Europe’ ‌and ‘Team ‌Ukraine’.”

Kyiv is eager for support from European allies, but Russia does not want European countries involved in direct negotiations, arguing they are financing and supplying Ukraine’s military effort.

European leaders have discussed whether Europe should be represented by one person or a team.

Supporters of a single envoy, like Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni, argue that the absence of a united European voice has allowed individual countries or small groups to engage in freelance diplomacy.

“There are too many different groupings discussing the issue,” she said.

The EU’s top diplomat Kaja Kallas, a former prime minister of Estonia, laid claim to the envoy role on Friday, saying, “I’m the one who is representing Europe in the foreign and security policy.”

“I know that the Russians don’t want me, but, you know, do we have a say, ‘Who is representing Russia?’” she said. “We can’t send any person that has no institutional role like the Americans are sending.”

Al Jazeera’s Milena Veselinovic, reporting from the summit in Dublin, said: “Kaja Kallas is putting herself forward for that role and for many she would be the natural choice – she is the voice for the EU on foreign policy.”

However, “there isn’t unanimous support behind her”, as Kallas is seen by many as “uncompromising” on Russia, she added.

Kallas is far from the only player in this game; European Council President Antonio Costa is also a top contender for the role.

US and Russia seek clarity on European voice

US and Russian diplomats have criticised Europe for not being united.

After the US-brokered talks between Ukraine and Russia in the United Arab Emirates this week, US envoy Jared Kushner said that “if Europe could identify one person to speak on their behalf, that would be a bigger achievement than getting the Russians to include them in the negotiation.”

Al Jazeera’s Yulia Shapovalova, reporting from Moscow, said the Kremlin has not confirmed that Putin agreed to expand the trilateral talks to include Europe.

Even though Russian officials say they are ready to talk with European leaders, they have also criticised Europe, our correspondent said, noting that Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov has even compared European leaders to “spiders in a jar”.

“During the Thursday meeting here at the Kremlin, the Russian side spoke about a revision of security architecture in Europe,” Shapovalova said. But “at the same time, Moscow refuses to keep EU leaders at the negotiating table during the peace talks,” she noted.

articles.title: Truck and bus crash in India’s Assam state kills at least 24 people
articles.summary: Several children and the bus driver were among those killed, officials said, with the death toll expected to rise.
articles.body:
At least 24 people have been ⁠⁠killed and 11 others injured, after a container truck collided with a bus in ⁠⁠India’s northeastern state of Assam, police said.

The crash happened on Friday on a highway in Golaghat district, near Kaziranga National Park, a UNESCO World Heritage Site famous for its one-horned rhinos, about 225km (140 miles) east of the state capital, Dispur.

Several children and the bus driver were among the dead, officials said, as Assam Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma said on X he was “deeply distressed by the tragic accident”.

“The scale of this loss has shaken all of us, and my heart goes out to every family that has lost a loved one. No words can ease their pain, but I want them to know that they are not alone. All of Assam stands with them in this hour of grief,” Sarma said.

He added that local authorities were at the site and “personally overseeing the relief arrangements … to make sure the injured receive the best possible medical care without delay”.

Swapnaneel Deka, superintendent of police of Golaghat district, told the Reuters news agency that “it is likely the death toll will increase”. He said the bus ⁠⁠was travelling to a neighbouring district, with about 30 people on board.

India has one of the highest rates of road fatalities in the world, with accidents happening regularly in part due to poorly maintained roads and vehicles .

articles.title: Kushner: Russia has agreed to include Europe in Ukraine war talks
articles.summary: U.S. envoy Jared Kushner announced Thursday that Russia has agreed to European participation in direct negotiations to end the Russia-Ukraine war, after three days of talks with delegations from both sides of the conflict. In the past, Russian leadership has opposed European diplomatic involvement, citing Europe’s financial support for Ukraine in the ongoing war effort. …
articles.body:
U.S. envoy Jared Kushner announced Thursday that Russia has agreed to European participation in direct negotiations to end the Russia-Ukraine war, after three days of talks with delegations from both sides of the conflict.

In the past, Russian leadership has opposed European diplomatic involvement, citing Europe’s financial support for Ukraine in the ongoing war effort.

“Both sides have now agreed to expand the next round of negotiations to include our European partners,” Kushner, President Trump’s son-in-law, wrote in a statement shared on social media.

“This will allow us to address the broader postwar European security arrangements alongside the territorial issues between Ukraine and Russia,” Kushner continued. “A lasting end to the fighting requires credible security guarantees, deconfliction mechanisms, and reciprocal de-escalation commitments that reduce the risk of future conflict.”

Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov offered a less certain commitment, saying on Friday that Europe must display its commitment to ensuring peace before Russia will let them join direct negotiations.

“Once we understand their genuine intention and readiness to contribute to the peace process, then it will be possible to make a decision on holding dialogue on a Ukrainian settlement in an expanded format,” Peskov said, according to Reuters .

European diplomats were present during the three days of trilateral talks involving delegations from the U.S., Russia and Ukraine in Abu Dhabi this week, but they remained on the sidelines.

The U.S. and Ukraine have pushed for European countries to appoint an individual representative to engage in direct negotiations.

Peskov indicated the Kremlin’s openness to contact with a European leader before agreeing to include a European representative in direct negotiations. However, he declined to comment when asked directly on Friday whether the government would welcome French President Emmanuel Macron in this role.

“Every hour, reports are appearing that name completely different candidates,” he told Reuters. “So for the time being we are not in a position to say anything specific.”

The Kremlin spokesperson also declined to comment on whether his government would accept European Union policy chief Kaja Kallas as Europe’s representative for direct talks.

In Friday remarks in Dublin, Kallas cast doubt on Russia’s ability to follow through on its promises and stressed the importance of Europe being involved in peace negotiations.

“For any deal between Russia and Ukraine, for this implementation, we also need the Europeans,” she told reporters.

“That is why the Europeans have to be at the table,” Kallas continued. “But I hope we are not just at the table, but we are actually also really influencing the outcome of these negotiations.”

articles.title: Rosenberg: Uncompromising Putin ups demands for peace with Ukraine
articles.summary: The fact the question of European security now features in discussions is viewed in Moscow as a victory, BBC Russia Editor Steve Rosenberg says.
articles.body:
Russia's President Vladimir Putin says he wishes "eternal peace" for Ukraine.

That is the same Russian president who ordered the full-scale invasion of Russia's neighbour nearly five years ago and who continues to reject the idea of a comprehensive ceasefire.

And what, in Moscow's view, is a prerequisite for peace?

The Kremlin spelt it out after talks with US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner: "A new, long-term architecture of indivisible security and peace."

Translated from Kremlin-speak, it means Moscow wants to change the security set-up of Europe in a way that benefits Russia.

What Russia is pushing for is, potentially, the biggest change to European security arrangements since the end of the Cold War.

The Kremlin has put back on the table its controversial proposal from December 2021 – the "draft treaties" with the US and Nato which would not only have put the brakes on the alliance's eastward enlargement by giving Moscow cast-iron guarantees that, for instance, Ukraine and Georgia would never be allowed to join, but also rolled back Nato military infrastructure from countries of central and eastern Europe which became Nato members following the dissolution of the Soviet Union.

Western leaders dismissed such demands as an unacceptable Russian ultimatum. Two months later Moscow launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine.

The "draft treaties" were put away. Now they are out of the geopolitical filing cabinet, and being quoted again by the Kremlin.

What is more, Yuri Ushakov, Putin's foreign policy aide, has suggested that Moscow is about to "add certain new considerations" to its list of demands in light of Western efforts "to inflict a strategic defeat on Russia".

That does not mean, of course, that Western governments will accept them.

But the fact that the question of European security is featuring now in discussions on Ukraine is viewed here as a victory for Moscow.

"In December 2021 Russia actively proposed that Nato rethink the security system in Europe," wrote newspaper Komsomolskaya Pravda earlier this week.

"Having secured one victory by forcing the West to think about security, our diplomats need a second by making the West heed Russia's concerns about Nato enlargement."

The EU's top diplomat, Kaja Kallas, has called Russia's demands for a new European security architecture a "trap" designed to "shift attention away from a ceasefire".

"The sequencing of Ukraine-Russia talks is important," Kallas wrote on social media. "The priority should be securing a ceasefire, followed by a peace agreement. Only then can there be discussions on Europe's wider security architecture."

Europe's problem is that, right now, it is not at the table.

Moscow has had no desire to give it a chair. It has slammed European leaders for their military support for Kyiv and tough stance on Russia.

This week's peace talks in Abu Dhabi involved Ukraine, Russia and the US.

After his discussions in Moscow, Witkoff indicated that Putin had agreed to the idea of European representatives joining the next round of Ukraine peace talks.

But on Friday the Kremlin indicated a final decision on European participation had not been taken.

"Once we understand their true intentions and their readiness to facilitate the peace process, then it will be possible to take a decision about dialogue on Ukraine in a wider format," said Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov.

Zelensky welcomes US bringing Europe into Russia-Ukraine peace talks

Europe's security 'fundamentally reshaped' by war in Ukraine

Inside devastated front-line city that Russia wants Ukraine to give up

At the talks with Witkoff and Kushner he was sounding uncompromising and confident.

The Americans are knocking at his door and seeking a deal and the Europeans are contemplating contacts with him. Last month the leaders of Norway and Finland reached out and called him.

And next week in Shenzhen, China, on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Co-operation summit, Putin may have a separate meeting with Donald Trump and Xi Jinping. Russian media are already comparing them to the "Big Three" - Stalin, Roosevelt and Churchill - who met in 1945 to reorganise post-World War Two Europe.

And yet, after nearly five years of war, Russia has suffered huge losses on the battlefield.

The Russian economy is under increasing pressure.

Ukrainian drone strikes continue to target Russian oil refineries, sparking fears of new fuel shortages.

But, so far, none of this has convinced the Kremlin leader to end the fighting.

articles.title: Weekend storm brings season’s first widespread freeze to millions across U.S.
articles.summary: A departing storm brought more than a foot of snow to parts of New York State on Friday, while this weekend the nation will see its first widespread freeze event of the season.
articles.body: A departing storm brought more than a foot of snow to parts of New York State on Friday, while this weekend the nation will see its first widespread freeze event of the season. As of Friday morning in New York, 12.5 inches of snow had fallen in Hartwick, 12 inches in Burlington, 11.5 inches in Exeter Center and 10 inches in Cherry Valley. Multiple locations in the Catskills region of the state saw 3 to 7 inches of snow. The morning’s wet snow will gradually taper off throughout the day, as rounds of rain were expected to impact the I-95 corridor from Philadelphia to New York. Some minor coastal flooding was also possible in New Jersey along the Jersey Shore and up toward Cape May. This storm will head out to sea Saturday, but cold northerly winds behind it will create lake-effect snow, rain showers and light snow across the Adirondacks, Berkshires, and Green and White Mountains in the Northeast. The first big freeze Another storm this weekend will bring the first below-freezing temperatures to millions around the country. Chicago will see wind chill temperatures on Saturday and Sunday of 24 and 27 degrees, with New York seeing 34 and 40 degrees, Atlanta seeing 31 and 32 degrees and Tallahassee, Florida, seeing 35 and 32 degree wind chill temperatures. Frost and freeze alerts are in effect from eastern Oklahoma to the coastal Carolinas, stretching as far south as southern Alabama. Some of the cities under the frost and freeze alerts include Tulsa, Oklahoma; Little Rock, Arkansas; Birmingham, Alabama; Atlanta, Georgia, and Raleigh, North Carolina. Parade of Pacific Storms Meanwhile, on the West Coast, a storm on Friday coming in off the Pacific will bring heavy rain from northern Washington to southern California as heavy snow blankets the Sierra Nevada mountain range. For southern California, some isolated thunderstorms are possible, including for the Los Angeles metro area. Through Saturday, rainfall amounts will be up to 3 inches from northern California to southwestern Oregon. For the Sierra Nevada mountains, snowfall amounts will be as high as 12-18 inches above 6,000 feet elevation. The active pattern will continue through the weekend, with the next storm system set to come into the Pacific Northwest Saturday night through Sunday. Heavy rain for South Texas On Sunday, Southeast Texas into western Louisiana will see heavy rain capable of producing some urban flooding. Rainfall amounts will generally be 1-2 inches, but there could be some localized areas along the southeast Texas coast that could see 3-5 inches. The cities of Houston, Galveston, Beaumont, and Lake Charles could be impacted. A few strong storms capable of damaging winds will also be possible for southeastern Texas on Sunday, stretching from Beaumont to Brownsville.

articles.title: 'India will be my first destination... want to watch the Ganga Aarti in Varanasi and do sunrise yoga in Rishikesh': Pakistani travel vlogger Muskaan shares her dream India bucket list
articles.summary: A Pakistani travel vlogger living in Germany has been getting a lot of love from Indian social media lately after opening up about something she’s wanted
articles.body: A Pakistani travel vlogger living in Germany has been getting a lot of love from Indian social media lately after opening up about something she’s wanted to do for years: visit India.Muskaan, who documents her trips on Instagram at @muskaan.travels, has already stamped her passport in more than 20 countries. Even so, India is still sitting right at the very top of her travel bucket list.And she has a pretty personal reason behind it.In a recent Instagram Reel, Muskaan opened up about her dream trip, promising that India will be the very first place she flies to the moment she gets her German passport.“While I'm Pakistani, my heart belongs to Delhi,” she said in another reel, sharing just how much affection she holds for the Indian capital and the country itself.From Bollywood memories to a long-awaited India tripFor Muskaan, wanting to see India isn't just some random impulse. A lot of the spots on her list have been stuck in her head since she was a kid, watching Bollywood movies and imagining what it would be like to stand in those places in real life.In her video, she walked through all the experiences she’s hoping to check off during that first visit.She isn't just looking to snap photos at famous tourist traps, either. She genuinely wants to soak in the culture, the spirituality, the festivals, and the natural landscapes.The places Muskaan wants to visit in IndiaHer bucket list stretches across different corners of the country, with each stop bringing a completely different vibe.1. Taj Mahal, AgraCatching the sunrise at the Taj Mahal is right near the top. Seeing that iconic white marble up close in the early morning light is something she’s been hoping to experience in person for a long time.2. Lotus Temple, DelhiThis stop means something much deeper to her. Because Muskaan follows the Bahá'í faith, the Lotus Temple holds a really special place in her heart, and she hopes to spend some quiet, reflective time there. For her, this isn't just another sightseeing stop - it’s a deeply personal dream.3. Ganga Aarti, VaranasiShe’s also eager to watch the famous evening Ganga Aarti in Varanasi, ideally from a boat out on the water. Between the glowing lamps, the chanting, and the sound of temple bells echoing across the ghats, it’s the kind of evening that sticks with people long after they leave.4. Yoga in RishikeshRishikesh made the cut, too. Famous for its yoga retreats, meditation, and calm atmosphere right along the Ganga, it offers the exact kind of peaceful reset she’s looking forward to.5. Celebrating HoliMuskaan wants to dive right into Holi - all the flying colors, loud music, and chaotic joy included. Watching it happen on a screen is one thing, sure, but actually being in the middle of the celebration is something she really wants to feel for herself.6. Hornbill Festival, NagalandHer list also takes her northeast to Nagaland's Hornbill Festival. This annual gathering celebrates the state's tribal heritage through traditional music, dancing, local food, and crafts, offering a look at a side of India that plenty of foreign travelers end up missing.7. Living root bridges, MeghalayaOne spot that completely fascinated her was Meghalaya's living root bridges. Grown over decades by carefully guiding the roots of rubber fig trees across rivers and streams, these natural bridges had Muskaan genuinely amazed - she even wondered out loud how something like that could actually exist.8. A night under the stars in JaisalmerShe also dreams of camping out in the Thar Desert near Jaisalmer. Sleeping under an open, starry sky surrounded by endless sand dunes sounds like her ideal way to take in Rajasthan.Indian social media users have a message for herOnce the Reel started making the rounds, Indian viewers flooded her comments with warmth and excitement. People welcomed her enthusiasm to explore the country, while plenty of others jumped in to drop recommendations for spots she should add to her itinerary.The video also sparked a lot of wholesome conversations in the comments about the shared cultural roots connecting people on both sides of the border.Muskaan wrapped up her video by asking viewers to suggest even more places worth seeing. And let’s be honest - in a country as massive and varied as India, eight spots barely even scratch the surface.“India is the first country I'm going to”The line that stuck with everyone most was her promise to make India her very first stop as soon as that German passport comes through.After traveling across more than 20 countries, Muskaan has already seen a huge chunk of the world. Still, it’s clear that India is the one place she wants to experience with her own eyes, instead of just through old movies, photos, and stories.For now, it’s a dream she’s patiently holding onto.And going by the reaction to her post, there’s a whole crowd of people in India ready to welcome her when she finally lands.Get the latest movie news, reviews, and celebrity updates. articles.title: China’s great AI chip loophole: How American espionage stopped China — this time
articles.summary: How American intelligence uncovered a suspected Chinese spy operation targeting Nvidia's AI chips through Singapore and Malaysia data centers.
articles.body: China may have discovered a remarkably effective way around America’s restrictions on advanced artificial intelligence chips: obtain the processors through ostensibly legitimate companies in Singapore and Malaysia, exploit weaknesses in American export enforcement, and use personal relationships to influence the leadership of the world’s most important AI chipmaker. The unfolding Nvidia scandal raises the possibility that an elaborate Chinese intelligence operation came dangerously close to succeeding. Indeed, some of the technology may already have reached Chinese customers. Congress and the CIA will have to establish how much China got away with and who helped them defeat America. A SPY TOOK OUT NVIDIA’S CEO. HERE’S HOW AMERICA STILL WINS THE AI RACE The most troubling unanswered question concerns approximately 50,000 Nvidia processors whose locations could not be reconciled with the company’s reported inventory records. Nvidia later said it located hardware in additional warehouses, but full public reconciliation and independent verification of final locations remained unknown. These are not ordinary electronic components. Nvidia’s H100, H200, and newer Blackwell-family processors are among the most strategically important technologies underlying modern artificial intelligence. They help train the advanced models that can transform military intelligence, cyberwarfare, scientific research, autonomous weapons, and economic competition. BEYOND KILLER ROBOTS: CHINA'S REAL AI THREAT TO AMERICA IS ALREADY HERE, EXPERTS WARN President Trump has spent years restricting Chinese access to the most advanced versions of these technologies. Yet China’s intelligence services and commercial intermediaries may have identified weaknesses in precisely the system designed to keep them out. An Unexpected American Intelligence Success At the center of the controversy is Alice Huang, also known as Huang Le, a Chinese businesswoman associated with Megaspeed International, a Singapore-based company acquiring Nvidia processors for cloud-computing operations. According to reporting by The New York Times, American intelligence concluded that Alice Huang had been recruited by China’s Ministry of State Security, the powerful civilian intelligence organization responsible for foreign espionage and counterintelligence and advanced technology theft. That assessment deserves serious attention. The MSS has a long history of seeking valuable foreign technology, political intelligence, and relationships with influential individuals. American intelligence officers reportedly identified concerns about Huang’s activities and her relationship with Nvidia’s founder, Jensen Huang. This American intelligence work may ultimately prove more consequential than the surrounding corporate scandal. US ATTORNEY WARNS CHINESE ESPIONAGE IS 'EXTREMELY PERVASIVE,' SAYS BEIJING 'PLAYING THE LONG GAME' The individuals who uncovered the suspected operation have not been publicly identified. Their discovery nevertheless illustrates the importance of counterintelligence: detecting foreign activities that may be deliberately concealed behind ordinary commercial relationships. The public record does not yet establish whether Alice Huang actually transferred Nvidia secrets to Chinese intelligence, whether Jensen Huang knowingly assisted any intelligence activity, or whether their romantic relationship directly influenced illegal chip shipments to China. How the Export-Control Loophole Worked The apparent weakness involved the distinction between selling advanced processors directly to China and selling them to companies operating data centers elsewhere in Asia. Singapore and Malaysia have developed substantial cloud-computing industries. Companies in these countries can legitimately purchase American technology, install processors in data centers, and rent computing capacity to customers worldwide. For China, that arrangement potentially presents two opportunities. CHINESE BOT FARM CAUGHT RED-HANDED TRYING TO INFLUENCE HEATED AI DATA CENTER DEBATE First, processors ostensibly destined for facilities outside China might subsequently be physically diverted to Chinese customers. Such unauthorized reexports could violate American export restrictions. Second, Chinese companies might obtain access to advanced American processors without importing the physical chips at all. They could instead rent computing capacity in overseas data centers. Reuters reported on November 12 that Chinese AI companies were seeking additional overseas Nvidia computing capacity amid fears that Washington might close this regulatory gap. This loophole is strategically significant: China might gain access to restricted American computing power while leaving the processors physically outside Chinese territory. This second method is not necessarily illegal under existing regulations. It exposes a distinction between controlling the shipment of advanced processors and controlling who ultimately benefits from their computing power. The Mystery of the 50,000 Chips Perhaps the most disturbing disclosure concerns the discrepancy between Nvidia’s reported sales to Megaspeed through hardware partners and the inventory identified during subsequent examinations. Bloomberg reported a discrepancy of roughly 50,000 processors between Nvidia’s initial government tally and shipments made through hardware partners. While Nvidia subsequently said it found hardware during inspections of additional Megaspeed warehouses, the company has not publicly disclosed exact counts—leaving open whether every processor can be accounted for and verified against unauthorized diversion to China. The question Congress must resolve is not simply whether an accounting discrepancy occurred, but whether the processors can be physically identified, their serial numbers verified, and their locations traced. The financial scale is considerable. A November 11 letter from Senators Elizabeth Warren and Christopher Coons stated that Megaspeed had purchased more than $4.8 billion in advanced Nvidia AI chips since June 2024. Did American Authorities Fail to Act? An especially troubling aspect of the scandal concerns the American government’s handling of the investigation. Bloomberg and The New York Times reported that Nvidia representatives communicated with senior Commerce Department officials while investigators examined Megaspeed’s activities. Questions have subsequently emerged about whether enforcement inquiries were delayed, restricted, or transferred between government agencies. The Commerce Department denies improper handling of its enforcement responsibilities. On November 12, The Washington Post reported that Singaporean authorities had repeatedly sought American assistance in their investigation but received very limited cooperation. Singapore ultimately found insufficient evidence to establish wrongdoing by Alice Huang under its investigation, and barred her from returning. If these reports are confirmed, Congress must determine whether failures of coordination, inadequate regulations, bureaucratic delays, or inappropriate outside influence undermined enforcement. The Three Questions Congress Must Ask Jensen Huang Although Jensen Huang resigned as Nvidia’s CEO on November 12, he remains an indispensable witness. 1. Where are all of the 50,000 disputed processors? Congress should require a complete, independently audited accounting of Nvidia processors sold to Megaspeed and its affiliates, identifying chip models, serial numbers, purchasers, intermediate destinations, and ultimate customers. Huang should explain when he learned of the discrepancies, what investigations Nvidia conducted, and whether the company can demonstrate that restricted technology did not reach unauthorized Chinese customers. 2. What did Jensen Huang know about Alice Huang’s possible connections to Chinese intelligence? Congress should establish the chronology of their relationship, her access to Nvidia executives, and whether she obtained sensitive information concerning product plans, major customers, export licensing, or the company’s discussions with China. 3. Did Nvidia or government officials interfere with enforcement of export restrictions? Congress should examine all communications involving Jensen Huang, Nvidia’s legal department, senior Commerce Department officials, and White House personnel concerning Megaspeed, export licenses, and the suspected diversion investigation. FOREIGN SPY ‘HONEYTRAPS’ TARGETING AMERICA’S TECH ELITE SPARK ALARM AMID NVIDIA CEO SCANDAL Lawmakers should ask whether any enforcement actions were delayed or curtailed, who made those decisions, and whether political or commercial considerations overrode counterintelligence warnings. A Strategic Warning The Nvidia affair illustrates a broader weakness in American technology policy. China does not necessarily need to defeat American export controls openly. It may instead identify gaps between legal jurisdictions, exploit overseas cloud-computing arrangements, cultivate strategically valuable relationships, and benefit from failures of coordination inside the U.S. government. Such methods would be consistent with the Chinese strategic tradition of moulüe (谋略) — the use of indirect methods, calculated deception, and strategic manipulation to achieve objectives without direct confrontation. The greatest failure would be to treat this affair merely as a scandal involving a powerful corporate executive. articles.title: Driver who fled to Latvia after killing Keaton Slater jailed
articles.summary: Aleksanders Dolars is brought to justice after fleeing the UK when he hit Keaton Slater at 70mph.
articles.body:
A speeding driver who fled to Latvia after killing a 12-year-old boy when he hit him at more than 70mph has been jailed.

Aleksanders Dolars evaded capture for Keaton Slater's death for more than two years because there was no extradition treaty between Latvia and the UK post-Brexit.

He was finally brought to justice in August this year when he was brought to England to appear at Warwick Crown Court following a determined campaign by Keaton's parents.

Dolars, 23, was jailed for nine years and four months by Judge Kristina Montgomery KC who told him: "Your selfish and dangerous driving took his life."

The court heard Dolars had been driving at 75-76mph in a 30mph zone when he struck the schoolboy in Coventry, killing him instantly.

Keaton, a devoted Coventry City fan, was travelling home from school with friends on 14 June, 2024, and had just got off a bus.

He had stepped out onto Radford Road and prepared to cross but the court heard he would not have seen Dolars' BMW at that time.

As it approached him he attempted to run out of its way with no success.

Dolars, who bowed his head throughout the hearing, did not stop and fled to his native Latvia within days.

Keaton's mother Louise Slater told the court: "I cannot understand how anyone could leave a child who had just been struck and not stop to help him.

"That knowledge has added another layer of pain to an already unbearable loss."

His father Clint's statement was read out by the prosecution, in which he described arriving at the scene shortly after the collision.

"The fact I that arrived there and saw my son being covered up will haunt me for the rest of my life," he said.

"I don't know if I will ever escape the pain of that moment."

When it emerged Dolars was hiding in Latvia, the Slaters fought to bring him back to face the consequences.

They were supported by Taiwo Owatemi, the MP for Coventry North West, and met with the Latvian ambassador to get Dolars back to the UK.

In August this year, he was finally extradited and pleaded guilty to causing death by dangerous driving when he was brought before Warwick Crown Court.

It had been thought he could not be compelled to attend the sentencing hearing, but Owatemi said the judge had ordered him to appear in person following representations to the justice minister on the family's behalf.

Keaton's mother described her son as "funny, caring, loving and full of life" and said he "loved football more than anything".

"When Keaton walked out of our door that day, we expected him to come home.

"We never imagined that we were watching him leave for the last time," she said.

"It is not only Keaton who died that day. A part of all of us as a family died with him.

"Our lives changed forever, and nothing will ever be the same again."

She also read out a letter Keaton had written on his first day of secondary school as a letter to his future self.

In it he wrote about his dream of playing for a football team and passing his GCSEs.

The hearing also heard statements from Keaton's brothers, Kai and Josh.

"Losing Keaton has left a space in my heart that can never be filled," Kai said.

"Keaton's death didn't just take away my little brother - I'll never get to see the man he would be.

"Knowing that someone could leave the scene after what happened, I will never understand."

Josh, Keaton's half brother, said he "struggled to comprehend" what happened and was angry Keaton had been taken away.

"The defendant has left a trail of destruction that cannot be repaired and will be with us forever," he said.

Sentencing Dolars, the judge told him: "You must have known you had struck a pedestrian.

"You must have realised he would have been gravely injured."

She also said it was clearly not a "momentary lapse of attention" because immediately before he had been seen cutting in front of cars by using the wrong lane at traffic lights.

Speaking after they left court, the family said they were unhappy with the sentence Aleksanders Dolars received.

"They gave him the maximum they could but it's not enough is it?" his father said.

Louise said that as Dolars would only serve two thirds of his sentence in prison, he would be out in six years.

"I know afterwards he can't drive," she added. "That's good to know - he's not going to be on the roads doing it to another family.

"To be in prison for six years, I think he should've got longer. My baby only had 12 years on this planet."

Det Ch Insp Sam Lewis, who led the investigation, said: "Keaton was a 12-year-old boy, making his way home from school, and he should have been able to arrive back safely."

She said Dolars had been "travelling at excessive speed and rather than stop and help Keaton he just left and tried to avoid capture".

Bringing him to justice had been "extremely complex", she said, but "through plenty of persistence, hard work and patience we finally got there."
